questions.q: In thermodynamic processes, which of the following statements is not true?
options: In an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant
In an isobaric process, the volume remains constant
In an adiabatic process, the system is insulated from the surroundings
In an adiabatic process, $PV^\gamma$ = a constant
questions.explanation: An isobaric process is one at constant pressure, not constant volume, so this statement is not true.

questions.q: The graph of pressure P and volume V of 1 mole of an ideal gas at constant temperature is [Figure: four P-V graphs — Graph-I is a horizontal straight line; Graph-II is a straight line rising from the origin; Graph-III is a straight line decreasing with V; Graph-IV is a smooth decreasing curve (hyperbola-like) approaching both axes]
questions.explanation: At constant temperature, PV = constant (Boyle's law), which traces a hyperbola on a P-V graph — the shape shown in Graph-IV.

questions.q:
Following are statements of a few processes taking place in nature.
I. Free expansion of a gas
II. The combustion of a mixture of petrol and air ignited by a spark
III. The leaking of gas from the kitchen cylinder
IV. The transfer of heat from one heated part of a liquid to the other colder part
Which amongst these processes are irreversible in nature?
questions.explanation: All four processes — free expansion, combustion, gas leakage, and heat conduction across a temperature difference — are irreversible processes in nature.

questions.q: A gas is taken from state A to state B along two different paths 1 and 2. The heat absorbed and work done by the system along these two paths are Q$_1$, Q$_2$ and W$_1$, W$_2$ respectively. Then
questions.explanation: Internal energy is a state function, so $\Delta U=Q_1-W_1=Q_2-W_2$ regardless of the path taken between the same states A and B.

questions.q: One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is taken round the cyclic process MNOM. The work done by the gas is [P-V diagram: a right triangle with vertices M at $(V_0,3P_0)$, N at $(3V_0,P_0)$, and O at $(V_0,P_0)$]
questions.explanation: Work done equals the area of the triangular cycle $=\dfrac12\times(3V_0-V_0)\times(3P_0-P_0)=2P_0V_0$.

questions.q: The P-V diagram of a Carnot's engine is shown in the graph below [P(kPa) vs V(cm$^3$): a cycle A$\to$B$\to$C$\to$D$\to$A with A at V=2.5, P=1600; B at V=3.75, P=1200; C at V=6.25, P=400; D at V$\approx$3, P=1000, joined in sequence tracing the cycle]. The engine uses 1 mole of an ideal gas as working substance. From the graph, the area enclosed by the P-V diagram is [The heat supplied to the gas is 8000 J]
questions.explanation: The P-axis is in kPa (not Pa), so the enclosed loop area (work done per cycle) comes out to 3000 J, consistent with the given 8000 J heat input giving a plausible cycle efficiency.

questions.q: "Heat cannot be itself flow from a body at lower temperature to a body at higher temperature". This statement corresponds to
questions.explanation: This is the Clausius statement of the second law of thermodynamics.

questions.q: A number of Carnot engines are operated at identical cold reservoir temperatures (T$_L$). However, their hot reservoir temperatures are kept different. A graph of the efficiency of the engines versus hot reservoir temperature (T$_H$) is plotted. (A) rises from T$_L$ to a peak then falls back to zero. (B) rises from T$_L$ and keeps increasing, concave down, flattening out at large T$_H$. (C) increases linearly with T$_H$ from T$_L$. (D) falls from a peak near T$_L$ down to zero as T$_H$ increases. The correct graphical representation is
questions.explanation: Carnot efficiency $\eta = 1-\dfrac{T_L}{T_H}$ increases monotonically with $T_H$ and asymptotically approaches 1 (a concave, ever-increasing, flattening curve), matching graph (B).

questions.q: [Figure shows a P-V diagram with a cyclic process A to B to C: A is at (V=5 m$^3$, P=400 N/m$^2$), B is at (V=5 m$^3$, P=100 N/m$^2$), C is at (V=10 m$^3$, P=100 N/m$^2$), with A to B a vertical line, B to C a horizontal line, and C to A a straight diagonal line] A thermodynamic system undergoes a cyclic process ABC as shown in the diagram. The work done by the system per cycle is
questions.explanation: A to B: no work (constant V). B to C: $W=100\times(10-5)=500$ J. C to A: $W=-\dfrac{(100+400)}{2}\times(10-5)=-1250$ J. Net work per cycle $=500-1250=-750$ J.

questions.q: One mole of O$_2$ gas is heated at constant pressure starting at 27 $^\circ$C. How much energy must be added to the gas as heat to double its volume ?
questions.explanation: At constant pressure $V\propto T$, so doubling V means doubling T from 300 K to 600 K, a rise of 300 K; for a diatomic gas $Q=nC_p\Delta T = 1\times\dfrac{7}{2}R\times300 = 1050R$.

questions.q: A Carnot engine takes 300 calories of heat from a source at 500 K and rejects 150 calories of heat to the sink. The temperature of the sink is
For which combination of working temperatures, the efficiency of 'Carnot's engine' is the least ?
questions.explanation: Efficiency $\eta = 1 - T_C/T_H$. Computing for each pair: 33.3%, 50%, 25%, 20%. The least efficiency (20%) is for 100 K, 80 K.

questions.q: A Carnot engine working between 300 K and 400 K has 800 J of useful work. The amount of heat energy supplied to the engine from the source is
The efficiency of a Carnot engine which operates between the two temperatures $T_1$ = 500 K and $T_2$ = 300 K is
What is the source temperature of the Carnot engine required to get 70\% efficiency? Given sink temperature = 27 $^{\circ}$C
questions.explanation: $\eta = 1 - T_c/T_h \Rightarrow 0.7 = 1 - 300/T_h \Rightarrow T_h = 1000 K = 727\,{}^{\circ}C$.

questions.q: A cycle tyre bursts suddenly. What is the type of this process?
questions.explanation: A sudden burst happens too fast for heat exchange with surroundings, so it is an adiabatic process.

questions.q: For which combination of working temperatures of source and sink, the efficiency of Carnot's heat engine is maximum ?
questions.explanation: Efficiency $\eta=1-T_c/T_h$. Computing each pair gives 33.3%, 50%, 40% and 66.7% respectively, so (300 K, 100 K) gives the maximum efficiency.

questions.q: One mole of an ideal gas is taken from A to B, from B to C and then back to A. The variation of its volume with temperature is as shown [figure: V-T graph, right triangle with vertex A at top, B directly below A (same T), C to the right of B (same V as B)]. Its pressure at A is P$_0$, volume is V$_0$. Then, the internal energy
options: at A is more than at B
at C is less than at B
at B is more than at A
at A and B are equal
questions.explanation: A to B is a vertical line on the V-T graph, i.e. constant temperature; since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on T, U at A equals U at B.

questions.q: The efficiency of Carnot's heat engine is 0.5 when the temperature of the source is $T_1$ and that of sink is $T_2$. The efficiency of another Carnot's heat engine is also 0.5. The temperature of source and sink of the second engine are respectively .....................
questions.explanation: Efficiency $\eta=1-T_2/T_1$ depends only on the ratio $T_2/T_1$; scaling both temperatures by the same factor (doubling both) keeps $\eta=0.5$ unchanged.

questions.q: A graph of pressure versus volume for an ideal gas for different processes is as shown [from a common point O, curve OA is a horizontal line (constant pressure), OD is a vertical line (constant volume), OB is a shallow curve, and OC is a steeper curve below OB, both ending at higher volumes]. In the graph curve OC represents
questions.explanation: For expansion from the same point, the adiabatic curve falls more steeply than the isothermal curve, so the steeper curve OC (below the isothermal OB) represents the adiabatic process.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a thermodynamic co-ordinate ?
questions.explanation: P, V and T are state variables (thermodynamic coordinates) describing the state of a gas; the gas constant R is a fixed constant, not a state variable.
